Question: GPS-Denied Navigation for an Autonomous Drone

Scenario:

An autonomous aerial drone is deployed for disaster relief in an urban area. It relies on GPS for navigation, but due to tall buildings, GPS signals are unreliable. To ensure accurate positioning, the drone uses a hybrid navigation system combining:

  1. GPS Data (Unreliable in urban areas)
  2. Inertial Navigation System (INS) (Uses accelerometers & gyroscopes)
  3. Wi-Fi Positioning System (WPS) (Uses Wi-Fi signals to estimate location)

Task:

Write a Python program that simulates how the drone determines its final position using sensor fusion:

  1. Inputs:
    • GPS coordinates (latitude, longitude)
    • INS displacement (meters moved in x and y directions)
    • WPS estimated position (latitude, longitude)
  2. Output:
    • The corrected position of the drone using a weighted average:

Final Position=w1​×GPS+w2​×INS+w3​×WPS

  • Use the following weights:
    • GPS: w1=0.3w_1 = 0.3w1​=0.3 (Less reliable in urban areas)
    • INS: w2=0.4w_2 = 0.4w2​=0.4 (Accurate but drifts over time)
    • WPS: w3=0.3w_3 = 0.3w3​=0.3 (Reliable in buildings)

Hints:

  • Convert INS displacement from meters to latitude/longitude adjustments.
  • Use weighted averaging to combine the three navigation sources.
  • Assume small distances, so latitude/longitude changes can be approximated using: 1 meter≈0.00001 degrees latitude/longitude
